At first, David found it difficult to keep the habit. Little by little, things began to change. David wrote down every idea in a small notebook. For example, the sugar tax reshaped soft-drink recipes.

The pedestrian street looked quieter than usual that evening. David plans to study English harder this term. On Thursday evenings, David reviews the notes from class. Best of all, buy now pay later tempts cash-strapped students.

People around David often share different ideas about the pedestrian street. There are always more possibilities than we expect. David prefers rainy weather when running in the park. What's more, a second-hand shop sells worn boots.

Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. Leo always says that small steps matter more than big plans. What's more, she saved twenty yuan with a coupon.
David bought a coat online because it was much cheaper. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams.
